text: From the SanMitra Newsroom,
this is the Daily AI Brief for 11 November 2026.
First, today's top headlines:
DeepMind's AlphaProof Code formally verifies parts of
Signal's encryption.
Google makes Gemini 4 Carbon widely available.
OpenAI opens ChatGPT to business profiles and business
agents.
Alibaba opens a preview of Qwen4-Max.
Dassault Systemes to set up an ASEAN industrial AI lab
in Singapore.
Andhra Pradesh clears a Rs 31,387 crore AI data centre
near Visakhapatnam.
Hackers used AI agents to steal Tajik government
documents, researchers say.
Adobe brings AI agents into creative workflows.
Fireworks AI details a security incident that reached
secrets and model weights.
South Korea jumps to 10th in IMD's digital and AI
competitiveness ranking.
And now, the news in brief.
Our lead story today.
Google DeepMind has unveiled AlphaProof Code,
an agentic AI system that generated Lean proofs,
checked by machine, for core security properties of the
actual production code underpinning the Signal messaging
protocol.
The verified properties include forward secrecy and
authentication, and the proofs reach right down to the
compiled machine code.
The work paired AI agents with mathematical proof
methods and specifications written by people,
producing proof code that runs to millions of lines.
DeepMind describes it as a research proof of concept,
noting that the proofs address selected properties
rather than every conceivable attack.
Even so, the company says it is a strong signal that AI
could make formal software verification practical.
That would mean going beyond bug-hunting to offer
mathematical evidence that particular security
guarantees hold, a development that could matter for
cryptography and critical infrastructure.
Also today.
Google said Gemini 4 Carbon can now be accessed through
the paid Gemini API,
Google AI Studio and Gemini for business.
The model is also rolling out to Google AI Ultra
subscribers, both in the Gemini app and in AI Mode in
Search.
The company is positioning it for agent work that
stretches over long periods,
including complex coding, research and security tasks,
and describes it as its strongest model.
At launch, the price is two dollars per million input
tokens and ten dollars per million output tokens.
The wider availability brings Google's leading model to
developers and businesses as competitors in the US and
China release new frontier models at a near-weekly pace.
In other news.
OpenAI announced a beta called Businesses in ChatGPT,
which allows companies to claim and control their
profiles within ChatGPT.
Using a Business Hub,
qualifying firms can edit company information and
provide product feeds with pricing and availability
details.
They can also view aggregated data,
such as how often they are mentioned and how many clicks
reach their websites.
OpenAI is also launching Business Agents,
which give customers a way to ask a firm's agent about
what it sells and the services it offers.
The initial rollout is limited to eligible e-commerce
and online-service businesses in the US.
OpenAI said businesses will not receive individual
customer conversations.
Firms may soon have to curate how they show up in AI
assistants, as they already do on search engines and
marketplaces.
In China.
Alibaba has launched a preview of Qwen4-Max,
the top model in its upcoming generation of Qwen models,
TechNode reports.
The model takes images and video as input and can
process as many as a million tokens of context.
Users can try it through Alibaba's Token Plan
subscription, as well as in the Qwen app,
Qoder, QwenWork and QwenStudio.
The complete Qwen4 release has yet to arrive.
Because Qwen ranks among the most popular open model
families with developers globally,
its next generation carries weight far beyond China.
In Asia.
Dassault Systemes, the French software group,
has signed a memorandum of understanding with
Singapore's Economic Development Board to establish its
ASEAN Industrial AI Virtual Twin Lab in the city-state,
TNGlobal reports.
The lab will use AI and virtual twins,
which are detailed digital replicas of products,
factories and processes, for manufacturing and industry
throughout Southeast Asia.
Dassault intends to recruit more than 30 AI
professionals at the lab over five years.
The move strengthens Singapore's ambition to serve as
the region's centre for applied industrial AI.
Turning to India.
The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet has approved a 512 megawatt
green AI data centre worth 31,387 crore rupees,
to be built by AM Intelligence at Bheemunipatnam near
Visakhapatnam, The New Indian Express reports.
The cabinet also cleared land at Bhogapuram for a
giga-scale AI data centre by Reliance.
It also approved a 570 crore rupee Epack plant that will
produce equipment for AI data centres.
The decisions reinforce the Visakhapatnam coast as one
of India's leading hubs for AI computing infrastructure.
Around the world.
Researchers at the cybersecurity firm CloudSEK say a
hacking group with links to Kazakhstan relied on
autonomous AI agents to take more than 2,000 documents
tied to national security from Tajikistan,
Reuters reports.
The agents were reportedly built on the open-.
They were used to scout targets,
support the break-ins, write tailored software and
organise the stolen material.
The operation came to light because the attackers
mistakenly left a server open that held their
operational data.
The findings point to AI in hacking moving past phishing
and malicious code, toward agents that manage multiple
phases of an attack,
which makes defence harder.
Turning to the United States.
Adobe announced a wide-ranging expansion of its AI tools
spanning Creative Cloud, Firefly and GenStudio.
The company is extending its Creative Agent so it can
carry out creative workflows involving several steps.
New integrations will also allow outside agents to
operate within Photoshop, Illustrator,
Premiere Pro and After Effects.
Under a broader partnership with Google,
Adobe tools will appear in more Google products,
and Adobe users will get greater access to Google's AI
models.
The direction is moving away from AI that produces one
image or clip at a time,
toward agents that manage multiple stages of
professional production.
That could shorten turnaround for media and marketing
teams, with familiar creative software remaining
central.
Elsewhere.
Fireworks AI, which provides AI infrastructure,
has released more details on a security incident in
October that started at an outside cloud provider.
The company said attackers got into internal development
machines and viewed some account and billing
information.
In a limited set of accounts,
they also reached secrets,
datasets and model weights that were incomplete.
Fireworks said the incident is contained,
credentials have been strengthened and its investigation
continues.
It added that it has found no effect on its inference
and training services, which by default do not retain
customer data.
The episode shows that AI security must extend across
the full supply chain,
from cloud hosts to datasets and development tools,
not only the model itself.
In Asia.
South Korea rose eight places to 10th out of 70
economies in the newest IMD World Digital
Competitiveness ranking, the country's science ministry
said, according to Yonhap.
The ranking gauges how prepared economies are to take up
digital technology and AI.
The United States took first place.
Singapore placed second in the Asia-Pacific region,
China seventh and Japan 19th.
South Korea's rise follows substantial government
investment in AI computing,
talent and public-sector use,
as Seoul aims to rank among the world's top three AI
powers.
From the research desk.
In a paper titled World In-Context Learning for Agentic
Robot Manipulation, the researchers tackle a tension in
how robots learn.
Skills from training usually sit in a network's weights,
its internal parameters, and that binds them to the
setting where training happened.
In-context learning avoids this problem.
It means picking up a task from examples given while the
model is working.
But it has trailed behind,
because a demonstration recorded elsewhere reveals
nothing about the robot's present surroundings.
The researchers observed that this kind of learning
captures meaning, like the steps of a task and what
objects are for, rather than appearance,
so it transfers between settings.
In their method, a frozen model begins from a
demonstration and practises the task in a simulator or
similar environment.
It holds the resulting feedback in its context rather
than undergoing retraining.
To recap today's top stories.
DeepMind's AlphaProof Code formally verifies parts of
Signal's encryption.
Google makes Gemini 4 Carbon widely available.
OpenAI opens ChatGPT to business profiles and business
agents.
Alibaba opens a preview of Qwen4-Max.
Dassault Systemes to set up an ASEAN industrial AI lab
in Singapore.
Andhra Pradesh clears a Rs 31,387 crore AI data centre
near Visakhapatnam.
Those were today's critical developments across global
artificial intelligence.
From our bureaus covering World,
